notes.claim: Heat per second in a wire carrying a current is proportional to its resistance and to the square of the current.
In an inverse square relationship, doubling the distance cuts the intensity to one quarter.
With no static lift, a centrifugal pump's power varies with the cube of its speed, so cutting the speed by 20% cuts the power by about half (added for i7's pump screens).
Twice as far from a light source the illuminance is a quarter, because the r² term in the denominator is 4 instead of 1 (added for i7's light screen).
A polytropic process follows pV^n = constant, with n a constant (added for i7's gas screen).
For an ideal gas, n = 1 in pV^n = constant is the constant-temperature (isothermal) process, Boyle's law (added for i7's gas screen).
A copper wire's resistance and cross-section vary with the square of its diameter (added for i7's cable example).
A conductor's resistance is its resistivity times its length divided by its cross-sectional area (used again in i7's cable example).

sources.title: Joule heating | Definition, Equation, & Facts | Britannica
sources.quote: The English physicist James Prescott Joule discovered in 1840 that the amount of heat per second that develops in a wire carrying a current is proportional to the electrical resistance of the wire and the square of the current.

sources.title: Adjustable Speed Pumping Applications: Industrial Technologies Program (ITP) Pumping Systems Tip Sheet #11
sources.quote: In centrifugal applications with no static lift, system power requirements vary with the cube of the pump speed. Small decreases in speed or flow can significantly reduce energy use. For example, reducing the speed (flow) by 20% can reduce input power requirements by approximately 50%.

sources.quote: A polytropic process is one in which pVn = constant, where n is a constant.

sources.quote: For a gas modeled as an ideal gas, when n = 1, the process is a constant-temperature (isothermal) process.
